generatedCommentsNodes.comment: The logic in `PushDownAndCombineLimits` for handling `MvExpand` could potentially create infinite loops if not properly synchronized in concurrent scenarios. Introduce thread-safe guards or ensure this logic is executed in a single-threaded context during query optimization.

The `MvExpand` constructor now includes a `limit` parameter, but there is no validation if this parameter is used elsewhere. This could lead to inconsistencies if not properly handled across the codebase. Add validation in the constructor to ensure `limit` is non-null and non-negative when required.

The `writeTo` method in `MvExpandExec` contains an `assert limit == null;` which will fail if `MvExpand` has a non-null limit. This is problematic as the new logic allows `MvExpand` to have a limit. Remove the assertion or modify it to allow non-null limits when writing to output.

While several tests have been added to verify limit propagation to `MvExpand`, there is no test case where the limit is explicitly set to `null` or a negative value. This could expose edge cases in limit handling. Add test cases where `MvExpand` is created with `null` or negative limits to ensure correct behavior.

review_comment: This rule seems to cover more cases than simply LIMIT->MvExpand, which the other rule now covers. Presumably the iterative application of the other rules will cover this scenario already, so this removal is of no consequence. And presumably test coverage will pick this up if that is not the case.
